lines.text: Hold a button, and the robot drives to a meter in front of a tag, using nothing but the camera.
Drive to point needed a pose on the field. This one only needs the tag.
The camera reports the robot's position in the tag's own frame. We pick our tag's ID, and ignore the rest.
Three profiled controllers do the driving: one for distance, one for sideways, and one to square up.
Facing the tag means a half turn in its frame, because the tag faces out toward the robot.
It's one loop: read the tag, drive, yield, and repeat. The same shape you wrote in Coroutines.
If the tag disappears, it stops, waits up to a second for it to come back, and gives up stopped.
When the tag comes back, the profiles start fresh from where the robot is, so it doesn't lurch.
Three ways out: it arrives, it gives up, or it's canceled. Every one sends a stop on the way out.
One loop, and a stop on every way out.
